title: the quality-gate verdict artifact (--verdict-file, conventionally gate-verdict.json)
description: Written by kernel/respawnpack.js cmdGate() from kernel/lib/gate.js runGate(). A CI artifact: uploaded and discarded, never committed, and with NO reader in this repository — which is stated rather than hidden, because an artifact nobody reads is a place where drift is free. ⛔ NOT_APPLICABLE IS DECLARED, NEVER INFERRED (Scenario N): the shipped gate used to be four YAML skip-branches that reported green after running zero checks. `ran` and `checks` are what make that impossible to spell again. ⭐ K-09: `outcome` is the pack's ONE four-value vocabulary (kernel/lib/outcome.js), so the exit code comes from `exitCodeFor` like every other verb, and the gate's own richer word survives as `label` — a display field that nothing derives an exit code, a rollup or a refusal from.

outcome.description: The shared four-outcome vocabulary. NOT_CONFIGURED maps here to CANNOT_DETERMINE — at the same exit 2 it always had, because 'the gate could not establish anything' was never the same claim as 'the gate failed'.

label.description: The gate's own word for this same verdict, kept so no diagnostic precision is lost: NOT_CONFIGURED (a stack was detected but nothing meaningful could run) reads differently to an operator than a bare CANNOT_DETERMINE. COULD_NOT_RUN is a ROW word and never a verdict — one check failing to start makes the run NOT_CONFIGURED, because the question went unanswered.

declared.description: Whether the outcome was DECLARED by the project rather than derived. True only on the NOT_APPLICABLE branch, where the project explicitly opted out with a reason; the gate emits it as `false` elsewhere, which is why this is a boolean and not a const — the field is the ANSWER to 'was this declared', and on every other branch the answer is no.

evidence.description: The file whose presence proved this stack — detection is never assumed.

checks.description: One kernel/lib/outcome.js `result()` row per planned check. The first seven properties are the shared row contract every verb emits; the rest are the gate's own planning facts, which are what a reader needs in order to fix the row and are not derivable from it.

checked.description: How many commands this row examined: 1 for a check that ran, 0 for one that was never configured or could not start. A PASS here can never be 0 — `result()` throws on it.

domain.description: Which question the row answers, from outcome.js DOMAIN (integrity | coverage | install | gate). Every row a gate run emits is a gate row.

subject.description: What the row looked at: the command line for a check that has one, the root it was planned in when nothing was configured to run there.

exitCode.description: The CHECK's own exit code, from the project's own tool. Present only on a row that ran, and never confused with this document's `exitCode`, which is the gate's.

ran.description: The count that makes a vacuous green unspellable: an outcome of PASS with ran:0 is a contradiction the reader can see.

exitCode.description: PASS 0 · NOT_APPLICABLE 0 · FAIL 1 · CANNOT_DETERMINE 2, from kernel/lib/outcome.js exitCodeFor — the same map every other verb uses. Four outcomes, three exit codes: 'I could not tell' has its own.
